items.response: Typecheck came back clean with 0 errors, so the named export change is done. I left the other default export in packages/cli/src/version.ts alone, since your rule was about format.ts. Action: wait for your next task, and convert version.ts to a named export too if you want it.

Makes sense, probes are what keep traffic away from pods that are not ready yet. I don't know yet which health route the api exposes or which port the container listens on, so I won't guess. Action: open the api helm chart (deployment template and values.yaml), find the health endpoint in the api code, then add a readinessProbe and a livenessProbe, plus a startupProbe if boot is slow, with timings in values.yaml.

Sure, I'll start from what the repo itself says rather than guess at the setup. Action: read the README, package.json (package manager, engines) and any version pin files plus .env.example in ~/code/acme-platform, then install the right runtime and dependencies and run the dev/build checks, telling you about anything that needs a secret from you.

Agreed, rebuilding everything on every PR is wasteful. I need to see how the CI workflow and monorepo tooling are set up before choosing between affected-only filtering and a task cache. Action: read the CI workflow files and the monorepo/task-runner config, then propose affected-only runs with a remote or shared cache for build, test and lint, and a path filter so docs-only PRs skip heavy jobs.

I can't tell from here whether that change has been reviewed, and getting an infra change into prod while Priya is out is not something I'd rush or do by hand. Marco's rollout depends on it, so I'd get it through the normal reviewed path. Action: look at the diff on priya/acme-212-redis-sg and check for an open PR, then see what the repo's process is for infra changes and who needs to approve, and tell you what is blocking before anything touches prod.

Redelivery from the broker is at-least-once, so the job needs to dedupe itself. I'll read the current handler first to see what stable identifier the message carries. Action: open services/worker/src/jobs/invoice-reminder.ts, add an atomic claim keyed on that identifier before sending, and write a test that processes the same message twice and asserts only one reminder goes out.

Yes, by default next/image goes through the Next image optimizer at /_next/image, so the request hits our Node process, which fetches the remote image from cdn.acme.dev, resizes and converts it, and caches the result. The cached result is served on later requests, so it's not every avatar every time, but the first hit per size and format does go through us. The build we just ran did show the cdn.acme.dev avatars resolving through /_next/image. Action: check whether any avatar component passes `unoptimized` or a custom loader, and tell you how big the cache and the cold-hit cost are likely to be.

Noted on billing: I won't change billing code without your review, and I'll put that in the onboarding doc for dev too. The local setup section will cover copying .env.example to .env.local, pulling secrets from the 1Password vault acme-dev, and running pnpm dev at the root to start web, api and worker together through Turborepo. Action: draft the local setup section in docs/onboarding.md, checking the repo for the Node version and any other prerequisites before I list them.

It depends on where the bottleneck is, and I don't know how the worker is deployed or scaled today. Replicas are usually the safer lever, since a higher concurrency per process can overload Postgres or Redis or the mail provider. Action: check the worker's deployment and autoscaling config, current replica count and queue depth, and the database connection limits, then recommend replicas, concurrency, or both with the numbers.

I'll write it as plain SQL that runs as is. I need the real table and column names, the status value for paid, and the SQL dialect before I commit to it. Action: read the invoices schema and migrations, then write tools/sql/monthly_revenue_by_org.sql with paid totals grouped by org and month for the last 12 months and a running total per org using a window function.

Makes sense, Excel needs the BOM to read the accented names like Café Lumière correctly. I'll add it only for csv output and leave json untouched. Action: add a --bom flag to the invoices export command that prefixes the UTF-8 BOM to the csv stream, add a test that checks the first bytes with and without the flag, and run it locally with pnpm --filter @acme/cli dev.

I don't have the layout of the CLI tests in front of me, so I'd rather look than describe it from memory. Action: open the packages/cli test directory and its test config, find an existing command test with a flag like --json as a template, and walk you through how it's set up before we add the new one.

Swapping the three console.log calls to the pino logger now, and for routes/invoices.ts:88 I'll log only safe fields instead of the whole request body. I'll check that the NEXT_PUBLIC_ stripe var in apps/web/.env.example is the publishable (pk_) key and not a secret. For the worker: copy services/worker/.env.example to .env.local (not .env), get secrets from the acme-dev 1Password vault, run docker compose up -d db redis, then pnpm --filter worker dev. Action: make the logger swaps and the .env.example check first, then start the worker stack.

I'll commit only the paid-at column work and leave the CLI coloring and PDF changes uncommitted. Commits follow Conventional Commits, so it will be something like feat(web): add paid at column to invoices table. Branch names start with the Linear id, and I don't know the ticket number, so I won't make one up. Getting it live means getting Priya's branch through that path, not around it. Action: check whether a PR exists for priya/acme-212-redis-sg, get the CI plan output on it, and flag to the platform team (and Marco) that it needs their approval while Priya is out.

ERR_TOO_MANY_REDIRECTS right after Lena's auth route change fits a middleware problem where the new sign-in page URL is being treated as protected. That is a guess from the symptom, not confirmed. Action: read apps/web/middleware.ts and the moved auth pages, check that the sign-in URL is in publicRoutes and the after-sign-in redirect is consistent, and look at the staging deploy for #828, then tell you the cause before changing anything in Lena's work.

Action: update the copy in DeleteCustomerButton (title, description text and button label), and check the 409 error text still reads fine for archiving.

I don't know yet which auth provider the sign-in page uses, so I'd check before pointing you at a setting. Social login like Google is normally toggled in the provider's dashboard, not in our code. Action: read the login page and package.json to identify the provider, check git history for recent changes to the sign-in page, and then tell you exactly where to enable Google.

The generated SQL has to be applied before the field can show up, so I'll run the migration first. The API listens on port 4000 locally, so the check is against localhost:4000. Action: run pnpm --filter api db:migrate, start the api with its dev script, then curl http://localhost:4000/v1/invoices (adding auth if the route needs it) and confirm paid_at is in the response.

Replicas are the first lever here: the worker already scales with KEDA on queue length, 1 to 20 replicas at one per 50 messages, so a big backlog should already be scaling it out. If it's pinned at 20 or the replicas are not scaling, that changes the answer, and bumping concurrency from 5 only helps if the jobs are not bound by Postgres or Redis. Action: check the current replica count and the KEDA ScaledObject in infra/k8s/ for the backlog, then recommend raising the max replicas or concurrency based on that.

Two likely causes. The build error says a development key is being used in a production build, so the Production environment in Vercel probably has a test/development publishable key instead of the live one. The hydration warning is the due date being formatted in the server's timezone on one side and the browser's on the other, so it needs a fixed timeZone. Action: check which env var holds the key in the Vercel production settings (I can't change that without your access), and find the due date formatting in the invoices page and pass an explicit timeZone to it.

The API verifies Clerk session JWTs using @clerk/backend, and that code is in src/plugins/auth.ts. Action: open that file in the api app to confirm the details before I describe the flow more, such as how the header is read and what it returns on failure.

I'll implement it as a hook scoped to the org routes so it doesn't hit health checks or public routes, rejecting with problem+json when the header is missing or doesn't match one of the session's orgs. The Inter font is loaded in app/layout.tsx, so I'd load JetBrains Mono the same way with next/font/google, expose it as a CSS variable, and register it in the Tailwind v4 theme in app/globals.css. Action: add the font and the theme token, then apply font-mono tabular-nums to the invoice number and amount columns in the tables.

Uploads already go directly to S3 with presigned URLs from POST /v1/uploads, so the flow is: the form picks a PDF, requests a presigned URL, PUTs the file to S3, and then saves the resulting key on the expense. The health endpoint is GET /healthz and it checks Postgres and Redis, which suits a readinessProbe. For liveness I'd avoid the same endpoint, since a Postgres or Redis outage would make Kubernetes restart healthy pods, so liveness should be a cheap check. Action: look at the api chart for the container port, add readinessProbe on /healthz, add a liveness probe that does not depend on the dependencies, plus a startupProbe, with timings in values.yaml.
